risks.title: Exit depends on a tenant not yet secured
risks.message: The exit is refinance 'once the new tenant has been in for six months', but the application does not name a tenant or show a signed lease. The broker cites only general 'good tenant demand in the area'. The exit therefore depends on an event that has not happened. Within the 18-month term, a tenant must be found, then occupy the property for six months, then the refinance must settle. The credit submission must explain this exit, including current leasing status and a realistic timeline.

risks.title: Refinance case not demonstrated
risks.message: The refinance is to 'their bank', but there is no evidence of the bank's appetite or criteria. It is also unclear whether the property will have enough lease income and term to meet a mainstream lender's serviceability and lease-term requirements at the end of the term. The credit submission should show the loan would meet those criteria, for example by stating the expected rent and lease length.

risks.title: Valuation may not be Lender-commissioned
risks.message: The Fenwick Property Advisory valuation appears to have been obtained by the client or broker and forwarded by email. The value is described loosely as 'about 3.9 mil'. If the borrower commissioned the report, or it is not addressed to the Lender, it can support initial assessment only. Also confirm whether the value is on a vacant-possession or a leased basis, given the property appears to be untenanted.
